[3 tasks to cut + 2 to hold â€” from gissa, derived from a gap analysis of the open UI/sim tickets. Concrete, narrowly-scoped, NOT umbrellas. Foreman mints IDs/priority.]

TASK 1 â€” Copilot conversation BODY. lane app-gui, kind new, ~P2. The in-flight Copilot tickets (T-BL38 context bar, T-BL39 attribution) touch only the INPUT ROW; the message body users read is untouched. Scope: streaming/partial output rendering, per-message copy, error-state rendering (failed calls show distinctly), auto-scroll+scroll-lock, code/artifact block rendering. Coordinate w/ T-BL38/39 for the shared panel.

TASK 2 â€” Persistence + undo/redo for the new UI toggles. lane app-gui, kind fix, ~P3, depends_on T-BL41+T-BL42. The new toggles are session-only w/ no undo. Scope: persist across save/reload (BL41 glyph visibility, BL42 absorbed-sketch eye-toggle); undo/redo for BL41 relation-delete + BL42 tree-absorption.

TASK 3 â€” Sim result VISUALIZATION in the GUI. lane simulation(+app-gui), kind new, ~P3. Every sim ticket (BL04/16/17/18, V&V BL20) returns JSON only; users expect to SEE results. Scope: viewport colormap contours (stress/fatigue/thermal/buckling), spectrum plot panel for FRA/vibration (BL17), toggle+legend.

HOLD â€” do NOT cut yet, flagging for visibility (need a sim-core owner scoping convo first): (a) Multibody DYNAMICS â€” loads on moving mechanisms (joint reaction forces/torques, motor torque); BL16 is kinematics-only by design. (b) Thermo-mechanical COUPLING (thermal-stress) â€” combines BL04 thermal + structural; coupled-field solve is an architecture decision. Both need sim-core owner input before becoming tasks.
